title: Countable Hom continuity on families with a common cohomological lower bound
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category and $D(\mathcal A)$ its ordinary unbounded derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. An object $K$ has countable bounded-below Hom continuity if for every family $(L_n)_{n\in\mathbf N}$ in $D(\mathcal A)$ with a common cohomological lower bound $b\in\mathbf Z$, every coproduct cofan $\iota_n:L_n\to B$, and every $q\in\mathbf Z$, the canonical map $\bigoplus_n\operatorname{Hom}(K,L_n[q])\to\operatorname{Hom}(K,B[q])$, induced by postcomposition with $\iota_n[q]$, is bijective. There is no boundedness condition on $K$.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.12 and the Hom calculation in Proposition 6.8.14(2), with precisely the countable common-bound hypothesis extracted for the abstract telescope argument
